chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-Khazzāz, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ibrāhīm, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام.
That ʿAlī عليه السلام was brought, in al-Kūfah, a man who had stolen a pigeon, so he did not amputate him, and he said: “I do not amputate in the case of birds.”

key_terms.الطَّيْرِ: birds; the category mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.حَمَاماً: a pigeon or dove; the stolen bird in this report
key_terms.عَلِيّاً عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam ʿAlī, the Commander of the Faithful, whose legal judgment is being reported
key_terms.فَلَمْ يَقْطَعْهُ: he did not amputate him; he did not apply the hadd of theft

ai.seo_question: Is the hadd punishment of amputation applied for stealing birds in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling from Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام regarding theft. When a man who had stolen a bird was brought to him in al-Kūfah, he did not apply the hadd punishment of amputation, indicating that theft of birds did not fall under the circumstances requiring that penalty in this case.
